subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which character set uses more bits per character and can therefore represent characters from many of the world's languages?
questions.explain: Unicode uses more bits per character than ASCII, allowing it to represent a very large range of international characters and symbols.

questions.q: Which secondary storage type uses spinning platters and read/write heads to store data magnetically?
questions.explain: A magnetic hard disk drive stores data on spinning platters that are magnetised by read/write heads.

questions.q: Increasing which of the following would most directly allow a CPU to execute more instructions per second?
options: The size of the hard drive
questions.explain: A higher clock speed means more fetch-decode-execute cycles are completed each second.

questions.q: When adding the 8-bit binary numbers 11111111 and 00000001, what occurs?
options: The numbers cannot be added in binary
An overflow occurs because the result needs a 9th bit
The result fits exactly in 8 bits with no issue
questions.explain: 11111111 + 00000001 = 100000000, which needs 9 bits, so an overflow error occurs in an 8-bit register.

questions.q: What is the denary (decimal) value of the binary number 00101101?
Which formula gives the file size of an uncompressed bitmap image (ignoring metadata)?
options: width x height x colour depth (in bits)
questions.explain: Image file size in bits is the number of pixels (width x height) multiplied by the colour depth.

questions.q: In a bitmap image, what does increasing the colour depth (bits per pixel) allow?
options: A greater number of possible colours per pixel
A larger number of pixels in the image
questions.explain: Colour depth is the number of bits used per pixel, so more bits means more possible colours.

questions.q: What is the 8-bit binary representation of the denary number 200?
Which storage medium is read using a laser?
options: Optical disc such as a DVD
questions.explain: Optical media such as CDs and DVDs are read by a laser detecting pits and lands on the disc surface.

questions.q: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explain: One byte is made up of exactly 8 bits.

questions.q: How many bits does a single hexadecimal digit represent?
questions.explain: One hexadecimal digit represents exactly 4 bits (a nibble).

questions.q: When digitising sound, what does the sample rate refer to?
options: The length of the sound file
The number of bits used to store each sample
The number of samples taken per second
questions.explain: Sample rate is the number of samples (measurements of the sound wave) taken each second, measured in hertz.
